newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CRUDES CLIMB HIGHER IN GASOLINE-LED MARKET.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CRUDES CLIMB HIGHER IN GASOLINE-LED MARKET.

text.p: U.S. crude prices attracted mostly firmer prices Wednesday, ending the session modestly stronger on an outright basis and for domestic grades.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing wound down a choppy session some 20 cents higher at $20.15-25 a barrel.

Sharp rallying on the NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures market propelled the energy complex to gains. The shutdown of Exxon's 110,000 barrels per day (bpd) catalytic cracker in Baytown, Texas triggered buying, traders said.
For the grades, sour barrels held firm in both the prompt September and the second month October, with nervousness over the flow of Iraqi crude behind the uptick.

"You've got the good gasoline performance and excellent margins, and it doesn't look like a flood of Iraqi crude going into one area. People are looking at the prices and getting a little nervous," said a crude broker.
Numbers showed September West Texas Sour/Midland selling at stronger levels than Tuesday, and talked late some five cents better at a $1.39-36 discount.
October WTS/Midland moved in some 10 cents to sell Wednesday morning at a $1.75 discount from differentials closer to WTI -$1.85 on Tuesday, traders said.

For sweets, Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire moved at 28 cents under the NYMEX September settlement of $20.19 a barrel in the U.S. aftermarket window. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold between a 16-18 cents premium, mostly even from Tuesday.

Iraqi news focused on word the U.N. overseers approved a slew of new contracts to bring total approvals to 14, out of a total of 21 submissions. Barrel counts for all of the approved contracts is now 75.42 million barrels.
